newsitem.title: POLAND: Air Liquide in Polish steel mill venture.
newsitem.headline: Air Liquide in Polish steel mill venture.

text.p: French industrial gas company Air Liquide will form a joint venture with the oxygen department of Poland's state-owned Huta Katowice steel mill, the mill's spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"Negotiations are going on...but the plan is for the venture to start activity on January 1, 1997," Renata Bytomska told Reuters, adding that Air Liquide would take a majority stake.
Bytomska said Air Liquide had offered to help in the production of storage and production facilities, including machinery producing gas at low temperatures.

She said the oxygen department, which employs 200 people and produces largely for the mill, required $350 million to $400 million in investment though it was not yet clear how much would come from each partner or other sources such as loans.
Bytomska said the mill was also negotiating the forming of a joint venture with Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB and several domestic firms.
She said the entire Huta katowice mill, which employs 22,000, made a net profit of 28.5 million zlotys last year on sales of 3.2 billion zlotys.
Earlier this year Belgium's Sidmar NV steel producer, a unit of Arbed, signed a letter of intent with Huta Katowice to build an installation for continuous casting and rolling.
